cls: Selective COX-2 inhibitor (coxib); injectable prodrug of valdecoxib
pharm: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory / analgesic for short-term postoperative pain
quick: 40 mg IV/IM once, then 20-40 mg every 6-12 h; max 80 mg/day
Reduce in moderate; contraindicated in severe
BP, renal function, GI symptoms, skin reactions
summary: Parecoxib is a parenteral (IV/IM) prodrug rapidly converted to the active selective COX-2 inhibitor valdecoxib, licensed in the EU for short-term management of acute postoperative pain. Usual dose is 40 mg followed by 20-40 mg every 6-12 hours up to 80 mg/day for no more than 3 days. As a coxib it carries cardiovascular thrombotic risk and is contraindicated after CABG surgery, in active GI ulceration and in serious cutaneous hypersensitivity. It is not FDA-approved; data derive from the EU SmPC.
indications: Short-term treatment of acute postoperative pain in adults

dosage.d: 40 mg IV or IM once, then 20-40 mg every 6-12 h as needed
Start at half usual dose; max 40 mg/day
dosage.n: Increased exposure; use lowest effective dose

dosage.d: Start half usual dose; max 40 mg/day

admin: Give as IV bolus or deep IM injection
Reconstitute powder with 0.9% saline or 5% glucose per SmPC
Do not mix with other medicines in the same syringe or line
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration (<=3 days)
Oral COX-2/NSAID may continue analgesia afterwards if appropriate
moa: Parecoxib is hydrolysed by hepatic esterases to valdecoxib, which selectively inhibits cyclo-oxygenase-2 (COX-2), reducing inflammatory prostaglandin synthesis and producing analgesic and anti-inflammatory effects while largely sparing COX-1-mediated gastric and platelet prostaglandins.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to parecoxib, valdecoxib or sulfonamides
History of asthma, urticaria or allergic reaction to aspirin/NSAIDs/COX-2 inhibitors
Active peptic ulceration or GI bleeding
Use after coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery
Established ischaemic heart, peripheral arterial or cerebrovascular disease
Third trimester of pregnancy and breastfeeding
monitor: GI symptoms and signs of bleeding

preg: Contraindicated in the third trimester (risk of premature ductus arteriosus closure and impaired labour). Avoid in the first and second trimesters unless clearly necessary; COX-2 inhibition may impair fertility and fetal renal function.
lact: Valdecoxib is excreted in milk. Use is contraindicated during breastfeeding.
renal: Use caution; coxibs reduce renal prostaglandins and can cause fluid retention, oedema and worsening renal function. Avoid in severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) and in dehydrated patients; monitor renal function in at-risk patients.
hepatic: Reduce the dose (start at half, max 40 mg/day) in moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B). Contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C).

major: Other NSAIDs/aspirin - increased GI ulceration and bleeding
ACE inhibitors/ARBs/diuretics - reduced antihypertensive effect and risk of acute renal impairment
moderate: Fluconazole and other CYP2C9 inhibitors - increased valdecoxib levels
interactions.food: Parenteral product; food does not affect dosing.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol; increases the risk of GI bleeding.
interactions.diagnostics: May raise creatinine and liver enzymes; can mask fever and inflammation.

rare: Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, erythema multiforme

monitoring: Blood pressure and signs of fluid retention
Skin for early serious cutaneous reaction (stop at first rash)
counsel: This injection treats short-term pain after surgery and is used for only a few days
Report any rash, blistering or mouth sores immediately and stop the drug
Tell staff about heart disease, stroke, kidney problems, ulcers or aspirin/NSAID allergy
Seek help for chest pain, weakness, black stools or vomiting blood
Avoid alcohol and other anti-inflammatory painkillers while treated
pk: Store powder below 30 C; use reconstituted solution promptly
pearls: Not FDA-approved; approved in the EU (SmPC) and many regions - withdrawn from the US with valdecoxib over cardiovascular and skin-reaction concerns
Prodrug rapidly hydrolysed to valdecoxib, the active COX-2 inhibitor
Limit to short-term use (<=3 days) at the lowest effective dose
Serious skin reactions can occur early - stop at the first sign of rash
missed: Given by clinical staff as needed for acute pain; there is no self-administered schedule, so a dose is simply given when pain control requires it within the dosing limits.
overdose: No specific antidote. Overdose may cause GI upset, drowsiness, hypertension, renal impairment and rarely GI bleeding. Manage with supportive and symptomatic care; valdecoxib is not significantly removed by dialysis.
